events.title: First Drone of the 2026 Wave Crashes in Lithuania
events.detail: A drone crossed into Lithuanian airspace and crashed near Lake Lavysas in the Varėna district, no damage reported. It marks the opening incident of a monthslong wave of drone and aircraft incursions into NATO's eastern flank. Analysts at the Warsaw-based Centre for Eastern Studies attributed the deviation to Russian electronic-warfare jamming during a concurrent Ukrainian long-range strike campaign against Russian oil-export terminals at Ust-Luga and Primorsk.

events.title: Drone Strikes Chimney of Estonian Power Station
events.detail: A drone flying in from Russian airspace struck the chimney of the Auvere power station roughly 2 km from the Russian border. No injuries or operational disruption were reported. Estonian Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna called the incursion 'a concrete consequence of Russia's full-scale war of aggression.'

events.title: Second Drone of the Day Crashes in Latvia
events.detail: A drone crashed in a field near Dobročina village, Krāslava Municipality, hours after the Auvere incident in Estonia. The Centre for Eastern Studies suggested the drone's intended target had been Russia's Ust-Luga export terminal before it was diverted by jamming.

events.title: Armed Drone Detonated in Controlled Blast Near Kouvola, Finland
events.detail: Two suspected drones entered Finnish airspace near Kouvola; one was found carrying an unexploded warhead and was destroyed in a controlled detonation. Ukraine's Ministry of Defence apologized to Helsinki and attributed the deviation to Russian jamming that severed the drones' satellite-navigation links.

events.title: Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania Reject Russian Claims of Complicity
events.detail: The foreign ministers of Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania issued a joint statement rejecting Russian allegations that the three states had knowingly allowed their airspace to be used to launch Ukrainian drone strikes against Russia, calling the claims part of a Russian disinformation campaign.

events.title: Tusk Announces Poland-Ukraine 'Drone Armada' Partnership
events.detail: Speaking at the Road to Ukraine Recovery Conference in Rzeszów, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk announced Ukraine would help Poland build a large-scale drone fleet, drawing on Kyiv's battlefield experience against Russian systems. 'Poland must have its own modern drone armada so that we can not only help Ukraine but also confidently tell Poles that we are safe,' Tusk said.

events.title: Drone Explodes at Latvian Oil Storage Facility Near Rēzekne
events.detail: Two suspected drones crashed near Rēzekne, roughly 40 km from the Russian border; one exploded at an oil storage facility, damaging four empty tanks. French NATO aircraft on Baltic Air Policing duty were scrambled. Latvia said the drones had been diverted off course by Russian electronic-warfare interference during a Ukrainian strike deeper inside Russia.

events.title: Drone Crashes Near Samanė Village in Lithuania's Utena District
events.detail: A drone assessed as a Ukrainian military unmanned aircraft crashed in a field near Samanė village. No damage was reported; emergency services activated their standard incursion-response protocol.

events.title: Latvian PM Forces Out Defence Minister Over Drone Response
events.detail: Prime Minister Evika Siliņa dismissed Defence Minister Andris Sprūds, blaming him for a slow rollout of anti-drone systems following the string of incursions. The move triggered the withdrawal of the left-leaning Progressives party from Siliņa's coalition, which accused her of scapegoating Sprūds.

events.title: Latvian Prime Minister Evika Siliņa Resigns
events.detail: Left with just 41 of 100 seats in parliament after her coalition partner walked out over the Sprūds dismissal, Prime Minister Evika Siliņa announced her resignation on national television: 'I am resigning, but I am not giving up.' It is the first NATO government destabilized, in part, by the 2026 incursion wave.

events.title: Romanian F-16 Downs Drone Over Estonia — First NATO Kill of the Wave
events.detail: A Romanian Air Force F-16 flying under NATO's Baltic Air Policing mission intercepted and destroyed a suspected drone over a field near Kablaküla, Põltsamaa Municipality — the first time an unmanned aircraft has been downed over Estonian territory by NATO in this incursion wave.

events.title: Drone Over Vilnius Halts Air Traffic, Shelters Lawmakers
events.detail: A drone violated Lithuanian airspace near Vilnius, prompting air-traffic controllers to suspend operations at Vilnius Airport. Lawmakers in session were briefly moved to shelter as NATO aircraft were activated to track the object.

events.title: Drone Detonates on Contact With Lake Drīdzis, Latvia
events.detail: A drone crashed into Lake Drīdzis in Krāslava Municipality and detonated on water contact with no advance warning issued to residents. Latvian armed forces deployed to inspect the site.

events.title: Von der Leyen: 'When the Baltic States Are Tested, All of Europe Is Tested'
events.detail: Speaking in Vilnius, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen called the drone incursions 'a deliberate strategy from Russia trying to destabilise our democratic societies' and called for a unified Baltic drone-alert system and a NATO-coordinated review of eastern-flank counter-drone and early-warning capability.

events.title: Russian Drone Hits Apartment Block in Galați, Romania — 2 Injured
events.detail: An explosive-laden Russian drone launched during an overnight strike on Ukraine crashed into the roof of an apartment block in Galați, roughly 10 miles from the Ukrainian border, and caught fire. A woman suffered first-degree burns and a boy suffered a panic attack. President Nicușor Dan convened an emergency defence council meeting and called the incident 'unprecedented'; Romania's Foreign Ministry called it a serious violation of international law.

events.title: Rutte Pledges NATO Will 'Defend Every Inch' of Allied Territory
events.detail: NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte spoke with President Nicușor Dan following the Galați strike and said in a statement: 'I affirmed that NATO stands ready to defend every inch of Allied territory. We will continue to enhance our readiness to deter and defend against any threat, including from drones.' He called Russia's actions 'reckless behaviour' and 'a danger to us all.'

events.title: Naval Drone Detonates at Constanța Port, Forcing Evacuation
events.detail: A floating object spotted near Pier 78 in the Port of Constanța was identified as one of four Ukrainian naval drones that had drifted out of control after Russian electronic warfare severed their guidance links. The drone self-detonated at 10:30 a.m. local time a few hundred metres from an oil terminal; the port was evacuated, forcing roughly 1,300 people out with no casualties. Two other drones detonated roughly 145 km east of Constanța and one remained under Coast Guard monitoring offshore.

events.title: French Rafale Downs Drone Over Berzgale, Latvia
events.detail: A French Rafale fighter on NATO Baltic Air Policing duty intercepted and destroyed a drone near Berzgale village in eastern Latvia. Latvia's military again attributed the incursion to Russian electronic-warfare interference redirecting the aircraft off its intended course.

events.title: Romania Joins NATO's 'Drone Edge' Joint Procurement Initiative
events.detail: Attending the NATO summit in Ankara, President Nicușor Dan announced Romania was joining the alliance's new Drone Edge joint drone-procurement initiative. Romania separately committed to raising combined defence and security spending to 3.7% of GDP in 2026, citing the year's repeated airspace violations.

events.title: Romania Faces Drone Incursions on Three Consecutive Days
events.detail: Romanian air defence recorded suspected Russian drones entering its airspace on Friday July 24 and Saturday July 25, the first two of what became a three-day streak of incursions along the Black Sea coast that culminated in a shootdown on July 26.

events.title: Romanian F-16s Shoot Down Drone Near Sulina, Envoy Summoned
events.detail: Two Romanian F-16s scrambled from Fetești airbase intercepted and shot down a drone over the Black Sea 12 km northeast of Sulina at 10:13 a.m. — the third drone downing in three consecutive days. Bucharest summoned Russia's ambassador to protest the 'repeated violations,' and President Nicușor Dan wrote: 'It is inadmissible and intolerable for the Russian Federation to continue violating Romania's airspace, which is, at the same time, NATO airspace and European Union airspace.'

events.title: Suspected Kh-101 Missile Crashes Near Lublin, Poland
events.detail: During a large-scale Russian missile barrage against Ukraine, an unidentified object entered Polish airspace at 03:40 local time; a quick-reaction F-16 was scrambled but lost radar contact with the object six minutes later. The object crashed in a field near Tarnawa-Kolonia in Lublin province, leaving a crater roughly 10 metres wide. Polish officials said the weapon was 'most likely' a Kh-101 cruise missile. PM Donald Tusk said he was 'in contact with NATO command and other European leaders regarding the violation of Polish airspace. Everyone declares full solidarity and readiness for any assistance.'
events.confidenceReason: Weapon type assessed as 'most likely' Kh-101 by Polish defence officials pending final forensic confirmation.

events.title: Polish F-16s Intercept Russian Il-20 Spy Plane Over Baltic Sea
events.detail: Polish F-16s intercepted and shadowed a Russian Il-20M electronic-intelligence aircraft flying without a transponder over international waters in the Baltic Sea. Poland's defence ministry called it Russia's latest attempt to probe NATO air-defence reaction times and radar coverage along the alliance's northern approaches.

events.title: Romanian Forces Destroy Two Drones Over the Black Sea
events.detail: Romanian air and naval forces destroyed two additional suspected drones in the Black Sea approach zone, bringing the total number of drone incursions into Romanian territory since the war in Ukraine began to roughly 29 — more than half of them recorded in the first five months of 2026 alone.

events.title: Explosive-Laden Drone Found at Leipzig/Halle Airport, Germany
events.detail: German authorities discovered a drone carrying explosives in a restricted area of Leipzig/Halle Airport — a cargo and NATO military-logistics hub used for the alliance's Strategic Airlift International Solution mission ferrying equipment to the eastern flank and Ukraine. The find triggered flight diversions, partial airport closures, and a counterterrorism investigation. Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt said the operation was 'carried out by professionals, probably on behalf of foreign powers,' calling it part of a hybrid-war scenario; U.S. intelligence officials told the Wall Street Journal they believed Russia was behind it. The Russian Embassy in Berlin denied any involvement.
events.confidenceReason: U.S. intelligence links the drone to Russia; the Russian Embassy in Berlin has formally denied involvement.

events.title: Germany Doubles Counter-Drone Unit After Leipzig Incident
events.detail: Following the Leipzig/Halle Airport incident, Germany announced its specialized Bundeswehr counter-drone unit would double in personnel to roughly 300 and expand from four operational bases to eight nationwide.

events.title: NATO Formally Assigns Russia 'Full Responsibility' for Incursions
events.detail: The North Atlantic Council met in Brussels to discuss the airspace violations in Poland and Romania and the wider drone-incursion pattern. Allies reiterated that Russia 'bears full responsibility' for the violations, calling them 'dangerous and unacceptable' and evidence of 'Russia's increasing tolerance for risk.' NATO pledged continued reinforcement of integrated air and missile defences from the Baltic to the Black Sea. Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov rejected the attribution, saying there were 'absolutely no grounds to blame Russia for this' and that Western officials should 'broaden their horizons' on drone sightings.

events.title: NATO Jets Shoot Down Drone Near Rugaji, Latvia
events.detail: NATO scrambled four fighters before dawn — two Italian Eurofighters from Šiauliai Air Base in Lithuania and two Turkish F-16s from Ämari Air Base in Estonia — and shot down a drone near the village of Rugāji in northeastern Latvia's Balvi Municipality, close to the Russian border. Finland separately restricted air traffic over the Gulf of Finland as a precaution. On August 20, Latvia's National Armed Forces confirmed the drone was Ukrainian-made, saying it "most likely entered the country's airspace as a result of electronic warfare interference, which caused the drone to deviate from its intended course" — attributing the incursion to Russian jamming rather than a Russian-launched weapon.

media.caption: F-16 Fighting Falcons on a NATO Baltic Air Policing sortie

events.confidenceReason: Latvia's National Armed Forces confirmed on Aug 20 the drone was Ukrainian in origin, redirected by Russian electronic-warfare jamming rather than Russian-launched.

events.title: Spanish F/A-18s Shoot Down Drone Over Romania Near Moldova Border
events.detail: Romanian surveillance detected an aerial target at 4:44 a.m. roughly 24 km north of Galați, approaching from the direction of Moldova. Two Spanish F/A-18 fighters, deployed to Romania on a NATO air-policing rotation and coordinated through NATO's Combined Air Operations Center in Torrejón, Spain, established radar contact and were authorized to engage, downing the drone at 5:01 a.m. over an unpopulated area. NATO assessed the drone as Russian — the fourth drone brought down over Romanian territory in 2026.

events.title: Germany Opens National Drone-Security Research Centre in Cochstedt
events.detail: Two weeks after the explosive-laden drone was found next to a Ukrainian Antonov cargo aircraft at Leipzig/Halle Airport, Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt and Research Minister Dorothee Bär inaugurated the Drone Security Technology Centre at the DLR site in Cochstedt, Saxony-Anhalt, alongside state premier Sven Schulze. The facility expands Germany's existing National Test Centre for Unmanned Aerial Systems and will research, test, and develop technology to detect and counter unauthorized drones around airports, major events, and critical infrastructure. Dobrindt said the centre would 'significantly strengthen' Germany's ability to respond to hostile drones; Bär said the goal was to ensure 'unwanted drones over an airport, over a stadium — not with us.'

media.caption: Federal Police drone at Leipzig Airport, August 2026

events.title: NATO Flies High-End Air Package With EA-37B Electronic-Warfare Jet Near Kaliningrad
events.detail: NATO and U.S. forces assembled a large air-defence package — an estimated 25 to 50 aircraft, according to unofficial observer counts — over northeastern Poland and the Baltic region near Russia's Kaliningrad exclave. The package included U.S. and Norwegian fighters, a NATO E-3A Sentry AWACS aircraft, a U.S. Air Force EA-37B Compass Call electronic-warfare jet operating from Powidz airbase in Poland and Souda Bay, Crete, aerial refuelling tankers, a U.S. Army ARTEMIS aerial-ISR demonstrator, and supporting Polish ground forces. NATO Allied Air Command said the alliance is 'a defensive Alliance and Allies are constantly honing their defensive abilities'; a U.S. official said the training ran across multiple days and was 'not triggered by specific Russian Air Force movement,' while Polish authorities described it as planned exercise activity.

events.title: Drone Crashes Near Grindu, Tulcea County After Entering Romanian Airspace
events.detail: Romanian military radar detected a group of aerial targets near the Ukrainian border at 02:23 local time. Two Spanish Air and Space Force F/A-18 fighters were scrambled to monitor the situation, and a Romanian Air Force IAR-330 SOCAT helicopter flew an aerial reconnaissance mission. At 03:21 a drone entered Romanian airspace roughly 13 km east of Galați; three minutes later the helicopter crew reported it had crashed approximately 4 km northeast of Grindu village in Tulcea County, in an unpopulated area. The impact sparked a small fire that self-extinguished; no casualties or property damage were reported. It was the second Romanian airspace incursion of the morning, preceding the Neptun Deep drone destruction by roughly three hours.

media.caption: Drone crash site near Grindu, Tulcea County, Romania

events.title: Romanian F-16 Destroys Explosive Drone Near Neptun Deep Gas Project — First Cannon-Kill of the Wave
events.detail: A commercial vessel radioed Romania's Coast Guard at 06:28 local time after spotting a maritime drone loitering a few hundred metres from the Neptun Deep offshore gas facility, roughly 80 nautical miles east of Constanța in Romania's Black Sea exclusive economic zone. Two Romanian F-16s were scrambled and one destroyed the drone with cannon fire — the Romanian Air Force's first gun kill and first engagement of a maritime drone. Defence Minister Radu Miruță said the drone was carrying explosives and that Ukraine had confirmed it did not belong to Ukrainian forces. President Nicușor Dan blamed Russia, calling it an 'intensification of these types of irresponsible incidents on the part of the Russian Federation'; European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen described it as part of 'an escalating campaign of threats' and 'hybrid warfare.' Neptun Deep is expected to make Romania the EU's largest gas producer when it comes onstream in 2027.

media.caption: Romanian F-16 jets deployed alongside NATO aircraft, August 2026

events.title: Drone Crosses From Moldova, Crashes Near Ciușlea Village in Romania's Vrancea County
events.detail: Romanian radar detected intermittent signals over Moldova's Cahul area shortly after 06:00 local time; one signal reappeared over Târgu Bujor, Galați County. Two Romanian F-16s from the 86th Air Base at Borcea and an IAR-330 SOCAT helicopter were scrambled — the alert ended at 08:52 with the helicopter finding no signs of impact or fragments on Romanian soil. Hours later, at around 8:30 a.m., a drone was found crashed into a walnut tree roughly 5 metres from a home in Ciușlea village, Garoafa commune, Vrancea County; the device broke into two pieces on impact. Authorities evacuated a roughly 300-metre safety perimeter. Mayor Laurențiu Diaconu said 'the area was isolated, and residents within the safety perimeter of approximately 300 meters were evacuated.' The Defence Ministry confirmed the drone carried no explosive payload and most likely originated from the Republic of Moldova. It marked Romania's 25th confirmed drone incursion of 2026 — nearly triple the nine recorded in all of 2025, according to the Ministry's own incident dashboard.

media.caption: Romanian F-16 and SOCAT helicopter respond to a radar signal over Târgu Bujor, Galați County

events.title: Spanish F/A-18s Scrambled Twice as Radar Detects Targets Near Snake Island and Vâlcove
events.detail: At 22:37 on August 24, Romanian radar detected two aerial targets 25 km northwest of Snake Island heading toward the Tulcea County border; two Spanish Air and Space Force F/A-18s from the 57th 'Mihail Kogălniceanu' Air Base were scrambled and a RO-Alert was issued to northern Tulcea County at 22:55. The contacts vanished from radar at 22:58 amid explosions reported on the Ukrainian side, with no penetration of Romanian airspace confirmed. The following morning at 07:31, a second aerial target was detected roughly 4 km east of Vâlcove (Vylkove), Ukraine, prompting another Spanish F/A-18 scramble and a further RO-Alert; again, no incursion into Romanian territory was confirmed. The back-to-back scrambles came hours after a separate drone crashed on Romanian soil near Ciușlea, Vrancea County, the same day — pushing Romania's 2026 fighter-scramble count to 47 situations, more than double the 21 recorded in all of 2025.

media.caption: Spanish Air and Space Force F/A-18 fighter, deployed to Romania's Mihail Kogălniceanu Air Base

events.title: Germany Finds Third Explosive-Laden Drone Near Leipzig/Halle Airport, Widening Antonov Attack Probe
events.detail: German investigators recovered a third drone and roughly 50 grams of suspected military-grade hexogen (RDX) in a field at Kabelsketal, just west of Leipzig/Halle Airport, on August 14 — ten days after the original August 4 incident in which an explosive-laden drone was found beside Ukrainian Antonov Airlines cargo aircraft at the airport, which hosts NATO's Strategic Airlift International Solution (SALIS) logistics mission, and a DHL cargo jet sustained minor nose damage after colliding with an unidentified object. According to NDR, WDR and Süddeutsche Zeitung, the new find suggests the plot involved more drones than first understood. German federal prosecutors had not publicly confirmed the explosive finding as of the report. Chancellor Friedrich Merz said those behind "hybrid attacks" against Germany "will pay for them," without naming a specific perpetrator; German security sources are examining possible Russian involvement, which Russia denies.

media.caption: Police at Leipzig/Halle Airport following the drone and explosives discovery

events.confidenceReason: The discovery itself is confirmed by multiple Tier 2 outlets and unnamed German security sources, but formal attribution to Russia remains unconfirmed by prosecutors and is denied by Moscow.
